device.name: ETEKCITY ESN00 Smart Nutrition Scale
device.notes:
The VeSync app is a multi-device platform. The ESN00 kitchen scale's own BLE interface is service 0x1910 with characteristics 0x2C10 (read), 0x2C11 (write / write-without-response) and 0x2C12 (notify / indicate), confirmed twice: by hardware reverse engineering (hertzg/metekcity, built from HCI-snoop plus noble against a real ESN00) and by the VeSync APK's own ESN00 code path (the mj0 BLE profile for BLE_MODEL 49314 = 0xC0A2). An earlier guess placing the scale on service FFA0 or FFE0 was wrong — those UUIDs belong to other VeSync device classes (the FFE0/FFFx map is the ESF-551-class body/fitness scale interface). The advertised local name is "Etekcity Nutrition Scale". FCC ID 2AB22-ESN00 (variant 2AB22-ESN002).
Frame format (both directions, big-endian): FE EF | model u16 (0xC0A2) | type u8 | len u8 | payload[len] | checksum u8. Total frame length is len + 7; checksum = (type + len + sum of payload bytes) & 0xFF. Example: fe ef c0 a2 c0 01 00 c1 sets unit g (0xC0 + 0x01 + 0x00 = 0xC1).
Commands (client to scale): 0xC0 set unit (1-byte enum), 0xC1 tare (payload 00), 0xC2 sync food/nutrition (36 bytes: 12 u16BE values scaled x10 — kcal, kcal-from-fat, fat, sat-fat, trans-fat, cholesterol, sodium, potassium, carbs, fiber, sugars, protein), 0xC3 query region, 0xC4 set backlight/auto-off timeout (1 byte seconds; app offers 30/45/60/120, default 120), 0xE5 set weight mode (APK constant in ESN00Command; no frame builder found — app-defined, unexercised). Reports (scale to client): 0xD0 weight (payload: sign u8 — 1 = negative, weight u16BE scaled x10: 0.1 g in gram mode, scaling for other display units unverified per hertzg's capture notes, unit u8, stable u8 — streamed continuously), 0xD1 unit state, 0xD2 battery (value / 10 V; app flags low at 2.4 V or less), 0xD3 tare state, 0xD4 region (1 = US; gates fl'oz unit availability), 0xD5 auto-off state, 0xE0 overflow ("Err", max 5000 g per the manual), 0xE2 low voltage, 0xE4 item-on-scale. Unit enum: 0=g, 1=lb:oz, 2=ml(water), 3=fl'oz(water), 4=ml(milk), 5=fl'oz(milk), 6=oz.
A working MIT-licensed parser/serializer is published as the npm package @metekcity/esn00-packet v2.0.0 (hertzg/metekcity monorepo, with a Web Bluetooth demo). The scale has no OTA update support (isSupportOta=false in the APK's ESN00DeviceProvider) and no firmware downloads exist from vendor, FCC or GitHub.
Research status: protocol confirmed by two independent sources — hardware RE with captured packet samples, and the APK's own ESN00 classes — that agree everywhere they overlap. No HCI-snoop gap remains.

credentials.notes: No WiFi passphrase is involved — the scale is BLE-only. A VeSync account credential is held by the app, not by the scale.

factory_reset.description:
Low confidence deliberately. The battery cycle is the only state change available on the hardware — the vendor manual covers weighing, units and cleaning, and documents no reset control — but nobody has established what, if anything, it clears. It is recorded as a procedure because it is the first thing someone holding an unresponsive scale should try, not because its effect is known.
If the goal is to hand the scale to somebody else, the thing that actually needs clearing is the app account, not the scale.
factory_reset.effect: Removing the batteries and reinserting them restarts the scale. No vendor source describes it as clearing anything, and there is little for it to clear: the scale holds no credentials and no bond, and user profiles and weight history live in the app account rather than on the hardware.

procedures.basis: The only state change the hardware offers; no vendor source describes it as a reset. A candidate, not an established procedure.
procedures.name: Battery cycle (candidate)

steps.action: Remove the batteries, wait a few seconds, and reinsert them.
steps.expect: The scale restarts. What this clears, if anything, is not established.

methods.description: Connect over GATT and read weight notifications directly, bypassing the VeSync app and account entirely. Corroborated by hertzg/metekcity's Web Bluetooth demo, which connects by advertised name and streams weight with no account and no bonding — a third-party hardware run, not one this project has reproduced.

steps.action: Place a load on the scale, or tap it, to wake it from standby.
Scan for the scale (advertised name "Etekcity Nutrition Scale") and connect over GATT.
Subscribe to report characteristic 0x2C12 on service 0x1910.
steps.expect: Weight reports (type 0xD0: sign u8 — 1 = negative, weight u16BE scaled x10, unit u8, stable u8) stream as the load changes.

setup.notes:
The scale itself needs no provisioning: it is a BLE peripheral that advertises and streams weight to whatever connects. The VeSync app asks for an account, but that is the app's requirement, not the scale's — the account exists to sync readings to VeSync's cloud, and nothing in the recovered service map suggests the scale is bound to it.
Hardware-confirmed: hertzg/metekcity's Web Bluetooth demo connects by advertised name and streams weight with no account and no bonding, and the vendor manual documents no pairing PIN or bonding flow. The scale is a single-connection BLE peripheral.

rejoin.notes: The scale joins no network, so there is nothing to rejoin. A new client may connect once the previous one disconnects.

characteristics.name: Scale Read
characteristics.notes: Read characteristic; in practice the streamed 0x2C12 reports carry the live data.

characteristics.name: Command Write
characteristics.notes: Command writes: 0xC0 set unit, 0xC1 tare, 0xC2 sync nutrition (36 B), 0xC3 query region, 0xC4 backlight/auto-off timeout, 0xE5 set weight mode (APK constant, no builder found).

characteristics.name: Scale Report
characteristics.notes: Reports arrive as notifications/indications: 0xD0 weight, 0xD1 unit, 0xD2 battery (/10 V), 0xD3 tare, 0xD4 region, 0xD5 auto-off, 0xE0 overflow, 0xE2 low voltage, 0xE4 item-on-scale.

services.name: ESN00 Scale Service
services.notes: The ESN00's only vendor service, confirmed by hardware GATT enumeration (hertzg/metekcity) and by the VeSync APK's own ESN00 profile (service 0x1910, write 0x2C11, notify 0x2C12). The unit also exposes the standard 0x1800 (0x2A00/0x2A01) and 0x180A (0x2A23/0x2A50) services. All commands and reports use the FE EF C0 A2 frame format documented in the device notes. (The FFA0 / FFE0 services previously listed here were misattributed from other VeSync device classes.)
